items.title: Lou Pallo interviewed by Monk Rowe, New York City, New York, January 14, 2007
items.q: And then with Gibson he worked with Ted McCarty and together they made the Les Paul guitar

ctx.x: Right. Well after all, I was never quite sure, what exactly did he — he invented the Les Paul guitar? What exactly was it that he did for the guitar? Do you recall?

Let’s see. I know he does have a patent on the trapeze tailpiece, that’s the bottom of the guitar. That he has a patent on. He did some innovation on, well the Les Paul guitar, more of a solid body, because he had what we call the railroad track, as he calls it, he put a string on the railroad track and the vibration of it and the sound of it sustains and so forth. That’s where you come in with the solid body. And then with Gibson he worked with Ted McCarty and together they made the Les Paul guitar, and that was…
Yeah. A pretty innovative guy, he did the stuff with the tape overdubbing.
